messages:
sam (eng-runtime): Noticed a weird tail-latency blip after yesterday's batching-heuristic tweak. p50 steady, but p95 jumped on streaming endpoints. Anyone else seeing this? :confused:

irene (eng-ml): saw alerts from customers -> increased tail. Which endpoints?

sam (eng-runtime): streaming/generate and chat-stream. Short requests (<= 64 tokens). Example numbers from canary A:
  p50 22ms -> 24ms
  p90 38ms -> 46ms
  p95 55ms -> 140ms
  p99 120ms -> 300ms

liam (eng-runtime): timeline: we changed the batching window from 8ms -> 2ms to lower latency. That reduced batch sizes; curious if that impacts host-side framing.

zoe (perf): i captured a perf trace and strace. Highlights: lots more writev/sendmsg calls, many ~512B frames. Also grpc stack shows frames without MSG_MORE set, so kernel flushes more often.

liam (eng-runtime): interesting. we rely on MSG_MORE to coalesce streaming frames into fewer syscalls. If code path bypasses MSG_MORE when streaming small chunks, syscall overhead spikes.

sam (eng-runtime): repro command I used against a canary:
```
vegeta attack -duration=30s -rate=400 -connections=200 -body=short.json | vegeta report
```

zoe (perf): pprof link (internal): https://pprof.internal/host/5891/stream-writev-hot

zoe (perf): top lines from pprof:
```
29.1%  writev/syscall
18.4%  stream_coalesce::emit
12.3%  kv_cache::lookup
9.7%   grpc_send_stream
```

irene (eng-ml): kv_cache shows higher miss rate for small batches? why would smaller batches cause more cache churn?

liam (eng-runtime): batching change reduces how often we touch the long-lived KV entries (we used to amortize lookups across a bigger batch). Now each request does its own lookup which increases L1 churn and more memcpys into tokenizer buffers.

sam (eng-runtime): combining both effects: smaller batches -> more frequent KV loads + uncoalesced streaming writes -> double hit on p95.

liam (eng-runtime): quick mitigation options:
- revert batching-window to 8ms (fast)
- re-enable MSG_MORE path unconditionally for streaming frames (medium)
- implement small-batch KV prefetcher (longer)

zoe (perf): i validated MSG_MORE patch locally: setting MSG_MORE on intermediate writes dropped syscalls by ~65% and p95 halved on the repro host. Patch sketch in my gist (internal): https://git.internal/gists/5891-msg-more

sam (eng-runtime): deploy-bot - canary rollback of batching-window change?

deploy-bot: Rolling back feature flag batching-window-small on canaries (hosts: canary-2..4). Started at 10:12.

liam (eng-runtime): while rollback runs, i'll open a small PR to always set MSG_MORE for stream chunks when response not finished; add unit test for coalescing and an integration wrk job.

zoe (perf): post-rollback canary numbers look better: p95 ~58ms (was 140). I'll run a 10m wrk to be sure and post flamegraphs.

irene (eng-ml): for medium-term, adding a KV-prefetch when batch size < threshold might help. Also we should baseline small-batch behavior in perf CI.

sam (eng-runtime): agreed. action items:
- immediate: rollback (in progress)
- short: land MSG_MORE patch + smoke test
- med: KV-prefetch prototype + perf CI for small-batch flows
- long: revisit batching heuristic with end-to-end perf budget (syscall cost modeled)

liam (eng-runtime): I'll include a note in the PR about kernel-selection interactions: if kernel selection forces per-request variant checks it can amplify small-batch effects. Keep that in scope for the postmortem.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed on canary group. Health checks OK.

zoe (perf): final quick numbers after rollback/MSG_MORE local test: p95 dropped to 50-60ms on canary samples. Will update dashboard and file a perf-regression ticket.

sam (eng-runtime): thanks all. i'll hold the batching-window rollout until we have MSG_MORE + KV mitigation in place. Posting summary to #release-war-room. :thumbsup:
